There comes a time when you want to extract every other row from your DataFrame. What I mean is: get the first row, skip the second, get the third, skip the fourth, and so on.

Say you have the dataframe below:

```{python}
#| echo: false

import polars as pl

data = {
    "Episode_Title": [
        "Pilot", "Errors and Omissions", "Inside Track", "Dirty Little Secrets",
        "Bail Out", "Tricks of the Trade", "Play the Man", "Identity Crisis",
        "Undefeated", "Shelf Life"
    ],
    "Release_Date": [
        "2011-06-23", "2011-06-30", "2011-07-07", "2011-07-14",
        "2011-07-21", "2011-07-28", "2011-08-04", "2011-08-11",
        "2011-08-18", "2011-08-25"
    ],
    "Director": [
        "Kevin Bray", "John Scott", "Kevin Bray", "Dennie Gordon",
        "Kate Woods", "Terry McDonough", "Tim Matheson", "Norberto Barba",
        "Felix Alcala", "Jennifer Getzinger"
    ]
}

df = (pl.DataFrame(data)
      .with_columns(pl.col("Release_Date").str.to_date("%Y-%m-%d"))
      )

df
```

<br>
And you want to select every odd-numbered row—like the first, third, fifth, etc.

I remember writing overly complex code with lambda functions just to achieve this.

## Getting every other row with polars

With Polars, you don’t have to torture yourself writing convoluted Python code. The `gather_every` function does exactly that.

```{python}
(df
 .gather_every(2)
 )
```

<br>
Isn’t that cool?

Even cooler ways to use Polars in my {{< var polars_course >}}!
